items.hook: Ancient Red Dragon is perfect for a playful encounter that can still punish bad habits.
items.body: With an Armor Class of 22 and 507 hit points, the Ancient Red Dragon presents a formidable challenge. Its commanding presence can disrupt party coordination, while its fiery breath weapon deals 26d6 fire damage in a 90-foot cone. Underestimating the dragon's 80-foot fly speed allows it to dictate engagement range, making it crucial to use terrain to limit its movement options. Forcing the dragon into predictable attack patterns can mitigate its battlefield control.
items.cta: DMs: Use a cliff or cavern ceiling to negate the dragon's 80-foot fly speed advantage and limit its fiery breath.

items.hook: The Order of Combat dictates that initiative determines turn sequence, not speed or dexterity.
items.body: Initiative, not dexterity modifiers or movement speed, decides who acts first in combat. Conflating dexterity with initiative leads to confusion when slower characters act before faster ones. This misunderstanding can disrupt strategy and timing. Planning actions based on actual turn order, determined by initiative rolls, prevents misplaced assumptions about character speed.
items.cta: DMs: Remind your players that page 13 clearly states initiative order dictates combat turns, not dexterity or speed.

items.hook: Wizard spells scale dramatically at level 5 with access to 3rd-level spells.
items.body: A Wizard's power spike occurs at level 5 when 3rd-level spells become available. Many players underestimate the impact of spells like Fireball, which deals 8d6 damage in a 20-foot radius. Mismanagement occurs when players rely on low-level spells or cantrips instead of utilizing these more potent options. Optimal play involves planning spell slots and positioning to maximize area effects and manage resources effectively.
items.cta: DMs: Remind your Wizards that at level 5, 8d6 Fireball beats cantrips, so they should stop hoarding spell slots.

items.hook: Low-threat on paper, high-chaos at the table: Bugbear Stalker.
items.body: AC 15 and HP 65 mean it can take a few hits while executing its plan. With a Stealth bonus of +6, it often surprises parties, making the first move count. Abduct allows it to reposition enemies easily, disrupting formations. Ignoring this mobility can lead to disastrous positioning errors. Focus fire on the Bugbear Stalker to prevent it from dictating the battle's flow.
items.cta: Players: laugh first, then respect turn economy before this joke encounter snowballs.
